title: Projection-neuron wiring in three fly connectomes predicts measured odour tuning of 31 to 45 lateral horn neuron types only weakly (mean r 0.13 to 0.17), but above chance in all five hemispheres
abstract: Question: does the wiring from uniglomerular projection neurons (uPNs) to lateral horn neuron (LHN) types predict their measured odour tuning, in different flies and sexes? Approach: we used whole-cell spike responses of 119 LHNs to 24 single odours (Frechter et al. 2019), each matched to a hemibrain body and type. We took signed uPN wiring per glomerulus from five hemispheres: hemibrain v1.2 (female), FlyWire v783 left and right (female) and male CNS v1.0 left and right (male). The glomerulus input was the DoOR 2.0 consensus response. A parameter-free linear model gave a mean Pearson r of 0.13 to 0.17 between predicted and measured tuning. The own-type prediction was better than other types' predictions (mean r 0.07 to 0.08; label permutation p = 0.002 to 0.034) and better than glomerulus-shuffled wiring (p = 0.001 to 0.014). A model that learns glomerulus inputs from held-out LHN types, without DoOR, gave held-out r 0.15 to 0.23 (p = 0.002 to 0.042) but near-zero explained variance. Type pairs with more similar wiring had slightly more similar tuning (Mantel r 0.09 to 0.16). Predicted tuning of one type repeated across the five hemispheres (mean r 0.75 to 0.93 versus 0.31 to 0.42 for different types), and measured tuning was reliable (median split-half 0.56). Thus feedforward uPN wiring explains a small but real part of LHN type tuning. Limitations: the input is a receptor consensus that agrees only moderately with measured PN responses; the model has no LH local neurons, other inputs or nonlinearity; all hemispheres share the same measured responses; a rank-based score was not significant at 0.05 in any hemisphere; male CNS results are weaker and not significant in two or three of six variant tests. Raw external data are not bundled; code, aggregate statistics and figures are.

display.caption: A: Mean Pearson r between predicted and measured odour tuning of LHN types in five hemispheres, for the own wiring (blue), other types' wiring (orange), glomerulus-shuffled wiring (grey diamond), and for the learned-input model with own (green) or permuted (grey square) wiring. p-values: label permutation. B: Hemibrain types: prediction r against split-half reliability of measured tuning (types with one recorded cell at left; marker size = recorded cells; dashed line = sqrt reliability ceiling).

A: Predicted tuning of the same LHN type agrees across hemispheres and sexes (blue) much more than predictions of different types (orange). B: Predicted tuning repeats across hemispheres (median r 0.85) and measured tuning is reliable (median split-half 0.56), but predicted and measured tuning agree weakly (median r 0.11, all types in five hemispheres).

A: Hemibrain LHN type pairs: cosine similarity of signed glomerular uPN input against correlation of measured odour tuning; line = octile means. B: Mantel r with the 95th percentile of a label permutation null in five hemispheres.
